high.title: This Week, Banks Intensively Hold Shareholder Meetings: 6 Banks Meet on the Same Day
high.summary: This week (April 20-26) marks the peak of the banking sector's annual shareholder meeting season, with multiple banks simultaneously holding meetings concentrated in 3 mid-week days. On April 21, PGBank opens the series at The Five Residences Hotel Hanoi. April 22 sees three banks meeting simultaneously: VPBank at Lotte Hotel Hanoi, SHB at Melia Hotel Hanoi, and Sacombank in Viet Tri, Phu Tho. April 23 has Kienlongbank hosting virtually. Most notably, April 24 is the climax with 6 major banks holding AGMs simultaneously: HDBank, TPBank, Vietcombank, VietinBank, BIDV, and MSB. The big three state-owned banks (Vietcombank, VietinBank, BIDV) will all meet on the same day, potentially creating significant market attention and impacting trading volumes as investors focus on their strategic announcements, dividend policies, and 2026 business plans.

high.title: Are Banks Short of Money?
high.summary: About 30 domestic commercial banks announced deposit rate cuts from April 10, with adjustments typically ranging from 0.1-0.5%. The list spans from major banks like Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank to joint-stock banks like Techcombank, VPBank, Sacombank, and SHB. In the interbank market, VND rates for the week of April 13-17 also dropped sharply across all terms. Overnight rates fell to 4%/year, down 2%, while 1-week, 2-week, and 1-month terms all declined simultaneously. While falling interbank rates usually signal easing short-term liquidity tensions, this doesn't fully reflect the deposit mobilization picture in the retail market where banks still compete fiercely for deposits. Despite rate cuts by 30 banks, high deposit rates persist in the market, indicating continued funding pressures and competition for retail deposits.

high.title: Techcombank CEO Receives Nearly 28 Billion VND Remuneration
high.summary: Techcombank published its audited financial report with notable personnel income figures. In 2025, the bank employed an average of 11,220 staff at the parent company, up slightly from 10,903 in 2024. Total employee income reached 6,326 billion VND, up marginally by 26 billion VND (0.4% increase). Due to increased headcount, average employee income at Techcombank decreased in 2025 to 47 million VND/person/month, down 1 million VND from the previous year's 48 million VND/month (approximately 2% decline). Average salary was 37 million VND/month, down about 4 million VND from 2024 (nearly 10% decrease). The salary fund decreased from 5,356 billion VND to 5,047 billion VND (5.8% drop), while allowances and other income surged from 944 billion VND to 1,278 billion VND (35% increase). This compensation structure reflects the bank's strategic focus on performance-based pay amid competitive banking sector dynamics.

medium.title: Total Market Margin Outstanding Debt Sets New Record, Securities Companies Lend Billions of USD
medium.summary: By end of Q1 2026, total lending outstanding (including margin and advance payments) at securities companies reached approximately 415,000 billion VND, up 9,000 billion from end-2025, marking a new historical record. Margin lending specifically reached about 405,000 billion VND, up 13,000 billion and also the highest in Vietnamese securities market history. This reflects strong investor appetite for leveraged trading amid market recovery.

medium.title: Before AGM, Sacombank Surprisingly "Changes Course" Canceling Proposal to Extend Restructuring Plan
medium.summary: Sacombank's Board of Directors unexpectedly canceled proposal No. 25/2026/TT-HDQT dated March 18, 2026 regarding extending the post-merger restructuring plan. The bank had previously cited difficulties in bad debt recovery and asset disposal requiring more time for legal procedures. The cancellation suggests improved confidence in meeting original restructuring timeline without extension.

medium.title: SJC Gold and Gold Ring Prices Afternoon of April 20
medium.summary: Afternoon April 20, domestic gold bar prices were adjusted down from early morning. SJC, DOJI, Bao Tin Minh Chau, Bao Tin Manh Hai, and Phu Quy all quoted gold bars at 168.3-171.3 million VND/tael, down 200,000 VND/tael buying price and 700,000 VND/tael selling price from morning. Gold ring prices also declined following the general trend, reflecting global gold price weakness.

medium.title: Q1/2026 Financial Results Update Morning April 22: Techcombank Reports 23% Profit Growth
medium.summary: Techcombank reported Q1/2026 pre-tax profit of 8,870 billion VND, up 23% from 7,236 billion VND same period last year. Other notable results included SJ Group (Sudico) with strong profit growth of 155% to 220 billion VND, Sonadezi Giang Dien up 22% to 85 billion VND profit, and Quang Ninh Thermal Power up 14% to 247 billion VND profit.
